overview: Explore top accredited institutions, tuition costs, eligibility, and visa procedures in Denmark for Winter Courses in Denmark.

universities.name: Technical University of Denmark (DTU)
universities.desc: DTU is offering three-week courses in January on a wide range of subjects within engineering, science and technology. Teaching in January 2027 will take place from 4 to 22 January. International guest-student eligibility and course prerequisites are to be checked on a case-by-case basis.

universities.name: Copenhagen University
universities.desc: Provides a variety of winter schools, research courses and pre-semester learning experiences. In January 2027, it offers winter schools in humanities and philosophy, some specifically geared toward PhD students and early-career researchers.

universities.name: Copenhagen Business School
universities.desc: Academic subjects are offered for students interested in computing and technology. The university lists single subject courses but applicants should check if a suitable course is available in the winter period and if external international applicants are eligible.

items.q: Can Indian students apply for Winter Courses in Denmark?
items.a: Yes, Indian students with qualifying credentials meeting English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) and academic prerequisites can apply to recognized universities in Denmark.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction for Winter Courses in Denmark?
items.a: Most master's and international bachelor's degree programmes are taught entirely in English for international students across Danish universities.

items.q: What are the typical tuition fees for Winter Courses in Denmark?
items.a: Tuition fees for international students generally range between DKK 60,000 and DKK 120,000 per year, depending on the institution and level of study.

items.q: Can international students work while studying in Denmark?
items.a: Yes, non-EU international students with a valid Danish residence permit are legally permitted to work part-time (up to 20 hours per week) during semester periods and full-time during June, July, and August.
